lede: Two events shaped it. A delegation of Christians rode into Madinah to argue about ʿĪsā, and were answered with the story of his mother’s family. And at Uḥud a victory turned to a rout within an hour, with the cry going up that the Prophet ﷺ was dead. Both ask the same of the believer: now that you have the truth, will you stay?

names.name: Āl ʿImrān
names.note: After the household it tells of (3:33–37): ʿImrān’s wife, who vowed the child in her womb to Allah; her daughter Maryam; and Maryam’s son.

names.name: al-Zahrāʾ
names.note: With al-Baqarah it is one of al-Zahrāwān, “the two radiant ones” — the Prophet’s own name for the pair.

revelation.detail: Al-Qurṭubī records agreement that it is Madinan. It was not sent down on one occasion. The commentators relate that its opening, to some eighty ayat, came down about the delegation of Najrān — sixty riders, led by the two men called al-ʿĀqib and al-Sayyid, who disputed with the Prophet ﷺ about ʿĪsā; Ibn Kathīr dates their coming to the ninth year. Its long central passage is about the battle of Uḥud, fought in Shawwāl of the third year. The traditional order places it eighty-ninth, after al-Baqarah and al-Anfāl.
revelation.when: Madinah — after Uḥud in the third year, with its opening tied to the delegation of Najrān

evidence.quote: ذَكَرَ أهْلُ التَّفْسِيرِ أنَّها مَدَنِيَّةٌ، وأنَّ صَدْرًا مِن أوَّلِها نَزَلَ في وفْدِ نَجْرانَ، قَدِمُوا النَّبِيَّ ﷺ في سِتِّينَ راكِبًا، فِيهِمُ العاقِبُ، والسَّيِّدُ، فَخاصَمُوهُ في عِيسى
هِيَ مَدَنِيَّةٌ؛ لِأَنَّ صَدْرَهَا إِلَى ثَلَاثٍ وَثَمَانِينَ آيَةً مِنْهَا نَزَلَتْ فِي وَفْدِ نَجْرَانَ

setting: The Christians of Najrān sent their leading men to Madinah. They came, the commentators relate, sixty riders strong, and pressed one question: if ʿĪsā is not the son of God, then who was his father? The surah does not begin its reply with ʿĪsā. It begins a generation earlier, with a woman — the wife of ʿImrān — vowing the child she carried to the service of Allah, and her dismay at the birth: “My Lord, I have delivered a female.” The girl is Maryam. She grows up in the sanctuary under Zakariyyā’s care, and he finds provision with her that no one has brought. Then the angels come to her with the news of a son. By the time the surah states its conclusion, the listener has watched the whole family grow: “The likeness of ʿĪsā with Allah is as the likeness of Ādam. He created him from dust, then said to him ‘Be’, and he was.”

When the argument was finished and they still held back, an ayah came down proposing something beyond argument: let each side bring its sons and its women and itself, and pray together that the curse of Allah fall on whoever is lying. Ḥudhayfah relates that the two leaders had come meaning to do exactly that, and that one said to the other: do not — by Allah, if he is a prophet and we do this, neither we nor our descendants will ever prosper. They asked for terms instead, and for a trustworthy man to be sent back with them. He ﷺ sent Abū ʿUbaydah.

The second event was Uḥud. The Muslims had the battle won; then the archers posted on the hill left their place for the spoils, the Makkan cavalry came round behind, and it became a slaughter. Seventy were killed, Ḥamzah among them. The Prophet’s face was cut and a tooth broken, and a voice cried that Muḥammad had been killed. Some sat down where they were. Nearly sixty ayat (3:121–179) go over that day — without softening it. “Among you were those who wanted this world, and among you were those who wanted the next.”

And at its centre: “Muḥammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?” Seven years later, on the morning he ﷺ did die, with ʿUmar refusing to believe it, Abū Bakr stood up and recited that ayah. ʿĀʾishah said: it was as though the people had not known that Allah had sent it down until Abū Bakr recited it.

The surah closes on the night sky. “In the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of night and day, are signs for people of understanding” — the ayat the Prophet ﷺ used to recite when he woke for the night prayer, looking up. Its last line gathers everything before it into four commands: be patient; outlast in patience; stand guard; and be mindful of Allah.

occasions.title: The mutual invocation
occasions.text: Al-ʿĀqib and al-Sayyid, the two chiefs of Najrān, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ intending to invoke a curse with him. One said to the other: “Do not do it. By Allah, if he is a prophet and we invoke the curse, we shall not prosper, nor our descendants after us.” They said: “We will give you what you ask of us; send with us a trustworthy man.” He said: “I will send with you a trustworthy man, truly trustworthy.” Then he said: “Stand up, Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ.” And when he stood: “This is the trustworthy one of this community.”
occasions.source: Ḥudhayfah: al-Bukhārī (4380). Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ adds that when the ayah came down he ﷺ called ʿAlī, Fāṭimah, Ḥasan and Ḥusayn and said, “O Allah, these are my family”: Muslim (2404).

occasions.title: Abū Ṭalḥah’s garden
occasions.text: Abū Ṭalḥah had more date-palms than any of the Helpers in Madinah, and the dearest of his property to him was Bayruḥāʾ, facing the mosque; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to go into it and drink its sweet water. When “You will never attain righteousness until you spend of what you love” came down, Abū Ṭalḥah stood and said: “Messenger of Allah, the dearest of my wealth to me is Bayruḥāʾ, and it is charity for Allah.” He said: “Well done! That is a wealth that profits.”
occasions.source: Anas ibn Mālik: al-Bukhārī (4554) and Muslim (998).

occasions.title: “You have no say in the matter”
occasions.text: On the day of Uḥud the Prophet’s tooth was broken and his head was gashed. Wiping the blood away, he said: “How can a people prosper who have wounded their Prophet and broken his tooth, while he calls them to Allah?” Then Allah sent down: “You have no say in the matter — whether He turns to them or punishes them.”
occasions.source: Anas ibn Mālik: Muslim (1791). Ibn ʿUmar relates it of his praying against certain men by name in the dawn prayer: al-Bukhārī (4069).

occasions.title: “Allah is enough for us”
occasions.text: “‘Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best to rely on’ — Ibrāhīm said it when he was thrown into the fire, and Muḥammad ﷺ said it when they said: ‘The people have gathered against you, so fear them’ — and it only increased them in faith.”

occasions.title: Praised for what they did not do
occasions.text: Some men of the hypocrites, in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, would stay behind when he went out on an expedition, and be glad of their staying. When he returned they made excuses to him and swore oaths, and wished to be praised for what they had not done. So there came down: “Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done, and love to be praised for what they have not done…”
occasions.source: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī: al-Bukhārī (4567) and Muslim (2777).

aim: Steadfastness upon Islam once it has been completed and made clear, and the answering of the doubts raised by the People of the Book — the Christians in particular.
themes: The clear and the ambiguous in the Book
A common word with the People of the Book
Holding fast to the rope of Allah
The day of Uḥud and its lessons

outline.title: The Book, clear and ambiguous
outline.summary: Alif Lām Mīm. Allah — there is no god but He, the Living, the Sustainer. He sent down upon you the Book with the truth, confirming what was before it; and He sent down the Torah and the Gospel. In it are ayat that are precise — they are the mother of the Book — and others that are ambiguous. Those in whose hearts is deviation follow the ambiguous. Those firm in knowledge say: “We believe in it; all is from our Lord. Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us” (3:8).

outline.title: The religion with Allah is Islam
outline.summary: There was a sign for you in the two armies that met. Made attractive to people is the love of desires: women, sons, heaped-up treasure. Allah bears witness that there is no god but He, and so do the angels and those of knowledge. The religion with Allah is Islam. Say: “O Allah, Owner of sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and take it from whom You will.” Say: “If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you.”

outline.title: The family of ʿImrān
outline.summary: Allah chose Ādam, Nūḥ, the family of Ibrāhīm and the family of ʿImrān above the worlds. The wife of ʿImrān said: “My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb.” Whenever Zakariyyā entered the sanctuary he found provision with Maryam. There Zakariyyā called on his Lord, and was given Yaḥyā. “Maryam, Allah gives you good news of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, ʿĪsā son of Maryam.” The likeness of ʿĪsā with Allah is as the likeness of Ādam. Whoever disputes with you about him: “Come, let us call our sons and your sons…”

outline.title: A common word
outline.summary: Say: “People of the Book, come to a word common between us and you: that we worship none but Allah.” Ibrāhīm was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but upright, a Muslim. Allah took the covenant of the prophets: when a messenger comes confirming what is with you, you shall believe in him. Whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will not be accepted from him. You will never attain righteousness until you spend of what you love. The first House set up for mankind was that at Bakkah; pilgrimage to it is a duty people owe to Allah.

outline.title: Hold fast, all together
outline.summary: O you who believe, be mindful of Allah as He should be minded, and do not die except as Muslims. Hold fast to the rope of Allah, all together, and do not divide. Remember His favour: you were enemies, and He joined your hearts. Let there be among you a community that calls to good. You are the best community brought forth for mankind. They are not all alike: among the People of the Book is an upright community. Do not take as intimates those outside your own.

outline.title: Uḥud: the morning, and the rumour
outline.summary: When you left your household in the morning to post the believers at their stations for battle. Allah had already helped you at Badr, when you were weak. Hasten to forgiveness from your Lord, and a Garden as wide as the heavens and the earth. Do not weaken and do not grieve: you are the uppermost, if you are believers. If a wound has touched you, a like wound has touched them; such days We alternate among people. Muḥammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him (3:144). How many a prophet fought, and with him many devoted men.

outline.title: Uḥud: what went wrong, and what was gained
outline.summary: Allah made good His promise to you when you were cutting them down by His leave — until you lost heart, disputed the order and disobeyed. Then He sent down upon you, after the distress, security: a slumber. It was by mercy from Allah that you were gentle with them; had you been harsh, they would have scattered from around you. Pardon them, consult them, and when you have resolved, rely on Allah. Do not think of those killed in the way of Allah as dead: they are alive with their Lord, provided for. Those to whom people said, “The people have gathered against you” — it increased them in faith.

outline.title: The signs, and the last command
outline.summary: Every soul will taste death, and you will be paid your wages in full only on the Day of Resurrection. You will surely be tested in your wealth and yourselves. In the creation of the heavens and the earth are signs for people of understanding — those who remember Allah standing, sitting and on their sides: “Our Lord, You did not create this in vain.” Their Lord answered them: “I do not let the work of any worker among you be lost, male or female.” O you who believe: be patient, outlast in patience, stand firm, and be mindful of Allah, that you may succeed.

keyAyah.why: The prayer of those firm in knowledge — and the surah’s own subject in a line: not finding guidance, but keeping it.

virtues.text: “Recite the Qurʾan, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for its companions. Recite the two radiant ones, al-Baqarah and Sūrat Āl ʿImrān: they will come on the Day of Resurrection as though they were two clouds, or two canopies, or two flocks of birds in ranks, pleading for their companions.”
virtues.arabic: اقْرَءُوا الزَّهْرَاوَيْنِ الْبَقَرَةَ وَسُورَةَ آلِ عِمْرَانَ

virtues.text: “The Qurʾan will be brought on the Day of Resurrection with its people, those who used to act by it; at its head will be Sūrat al-Baqarah and Āl ʿImrān.”

Ibn ʿAbbās said: I spent a night at the house of my aunt Maymūnah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ talked with his family for a while, then slept. When the last third of the night came he sat up, looked at the sky, and recited: “In the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of night and day, are signs for people of understanding.” Then he rose, made ablution, cleaned his teeth, and prayed.

Abū Bakr came out while ʿUmar was speaking to the people, and said: “Whoever among you worshipped Muḥammad — Muḥammad has died. And whoever worshipped Allah — Allah is living and does not die. Allah has said: ‘Muḥammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him…’” By Allah, it was as though the people had not known that Allah had sent down this ayah until Abū Bakr recited it; and everyone took it up from him.

before: Al-Baqarah ended with a prayer: “help us against the disbelieving people.” Āl ʿImrān takes up both fronts of that struggle — the argument with the People of the Book, and the battlefield.
after: Āl ʿImrān ends: “be mindful of Allah.” Al-Nisāʾ begins: “O mankind, be mindful of your Lord, who created you from a single soul.”
